## 2. Quality vocabulary, readiness and evidence

- **precedence**:

- **status_of_reason**:
  - **absent_input**: missing_input
  - **unknown_availability**: missing_input
  - **future_knowledge**: missing_input
  - **null_field**: missing_input
  - **ineligible**: missing_input
  - **governed_gap**: incomplete_coverage
  - **future_market**: incomplete_coverage
  - **partial_universe**: incomplete_coverage
  - **insufficient_history**: insufficient_history
  - **no_eligible_observations**: not_applicable
  - **empty_universe**: not_applicable
  - **zero_denominator**: not_applicable
- **rule**: all applicable reasons retained in lexical order; status follows the first applicable reason in precedence; a value is null exactly when the status is not available; available implies observed == expected
- **slot_causes**:
  - **no row and no coverage**: absent_input
  - **known_at null**: unknown_availability
  - **known_at > K**: future_knowledge
  - **row present with null volume (null OHLC) or null close in a close-only delivery**: null_field
  - **declared incomplete coverage**: governed_gap
  - **coverage-proven empty slot (zero volume, null OHLC)**: no_eligible_observations
  - **required column not delivered (high or low in a close-only delivery)**: absent_input
- **counts**:
  - **all_outputs**: expected = N + 1 slots; observed = READY slots among max(a, t-N)..t for the output's own fields; the reasons are the causes of the lost slots only; insufficient_history is added only when t - N < a (the epoch holds fewer than N+1 slots); an available row has observed = expected. Range outputs of a close-only delivery: the high and low of slots t-N+1..t are not delivered (absent_input) but the base slot needs only its close, so observed is 1 when the base close is READY (PE20)
- **unreachable_reasons**:
  - ineligible
  - future_market
  - partial_universe
  - empty_universe
- **evidence**:
  - **limit**: config evidence_limit 0..10000 is result-wide as FeatureResult bounds it; fixtures list the per-output witnesses when the output is selected alone; a joint selection concatenates outputs in lexical feature-id order and truncates
  - **order**: target slot first, then the base slot t-N, then slots t-N+1..t-1 ascending; unavailable outputs emit none
  - **row_id**: slot:<i> with i the R17 slot index of the epoch
  - **boundary**: completed_interval
